liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (5 reviews): Jack Straw is singled out as exceptionally hot, with Bruce Hornsby prominent throughout; Reviewer says Jack Straw is worth the download alone and doubts any better version exists [16][19][23][25][26]
- **Jackaroe** (2 reviews): Jack a Roe, Tennessee Jed and Promised Land are named as standout performances; Jack-a-Roe is a strong, powerful version in the first set [16][23]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Reviewer finds Tennessee Jed smokin' despite finding the first set low on energy [24]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Second set opens with a great China Cat into Rider [20]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): The China Cat into I Know You Rider is called nice [16]
- **Desolation Row** (1 review): Bobby Weir plays Desolation Row, and Bruce Hornsby's piano pushes the band to inspired playing [18]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): He's Gone is called out of this world; Truckin' > Spoonful > He's Gone is the highlight of the MSG run [20]
- **Let the Good Times Roll** (1 review): The opener is done well; Bobby and Bruce both hit a high note together [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **Beam**: rare: 5 archived performances [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-09-14.150163.sbd.cm.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 156 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1991-09-14.nak300.gidley.122035.flac2448**: audience recording; 21 songs; 153 min [3]
- **gd91-09-14.sbd.kowalski.522.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 153 min; rated 4/5 by 15 [5]. Said about its sound: The soundboard quality is described as fantastic [19]
- **gd1991-09-14.sbd.hinko.77789.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 156 min [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer once had an audience tape; the crowd was spectacular, maybe more exhilarating than the soundboard [19]
- Says Hornsby reported Garcia was uninterested then, and Bruce talked Jerry into giving full effort between the MSG and Boston runs [24]
- Reviewer sat in the taper's section; considers Hornsby on fire, his best show seen with the band [25]
- Weir kept signaling for the jam to end, but Garcia and Bruce smirked and kept playing [26]
- Reviewer wonders whether this show beats the 9/10/91 show at the same run [20]
- Reviewer prefers the 6-25-91 Jack Straw and Sugaree as the best of the Hornsby era [24]
- The 9-19-90 Jack Straw is ranked a close second among Hornsby-era Straws [25]
- Reviewer finds the show decent but with several off moments and flubs, not top-rated [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-09-14.150163.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  May 26, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [1]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several sets of masters were combined to complete the show [1]
- **gd1991-09-14.nak300.gidley.122035.flac2448**: taped by Ted Gidley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: OTS AUD: 2x Nakamichi CM300 w/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MXS 90/100, w/no Dolby. Taped by Ted Gidley. [3]. Also: Nakamichi 300 source with patches from the ID-25318 recording, covering crowd gaps at the end of Friend of the Devil and Jackaroe [3]
- **gd91-09-14.sbd.kowalski.522.sbeok.shnf**: source: sbd> dat> cd> eac> shn [5]
- **gd1991-09-14.sbd.hinko.77789.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Darryl Hinko; source: Clean up of SHNid=32904 by Darryl Hinko [7]. Also: Darryl Hinko cleaned up Charlie Miller's files with Cool Edit Pro, removing most bass buzz and joining tracks [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Madison Square Garden - September 14, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/september-14-1991) [29]
